name: toLocaleDateString-causes-hydration-mismatch
hook: toLocaleDateString causes hydration mismatch between Node.js and browser
body: toLocaleDateString output can differ between Node.js server and browser due to ICU data version differences or timezone discrepancies, causing React hydration error #418 (server-rendered HTML does not match client). Fix: use UTC-based manual date formatting with hardcoded month names instead of toLocaleDateString.
why: This bug manifested as a real production issue on the purchase detail page. The fix is applicable to any date formatting in Next.js server/client components.

name: translation-key-mismatch-status-vs-statuses
hook: Brand messages use 'statuses' plural, components used 'status' singular
body: StatusBadge and StatusDisplay components used t('status.{status}') but the brand messages define account.purchases.statuses.pending etc. (plural 'statuses'). The t() fallback returns the raw key when a translation is missing, which can cause server/client text divergence and hydration mismatches.
why: This is a common pattern: singular key for the field label, plural for enum values. The mismatch silently fell back to raw keys which could differ between server and client i18n resolution.
